intro: Before you stands Rumeli Fortress, a castle and walls in İstanbul province, built in 1452. It went up in just four months at the narrowest point of the Bosphorus, before the siege of Constantinople, with one purpose: to cut the city off from relief by sea.
history: Before the siege of Constantinople, Mehmed II built this fortress at the narrowest point of the Bosphorus, directly opposite Anadolu Hisarı. Construction took four months, in the summer of 1452. Each of the three great towers was assigned to a vizier, and each still carries his name. And the guns mounted here could stop any ship in the strait.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the great towers: Halil Pasha Tower, Saruca Pasha Tower and Zağanos Pasha Tower. Follow the curtain walls between them, and finish at the Amphitheatre.
facts: Did you know? While the fortress was being built, a Venetian ship that tried to run the strait was sunk — an act that effectively ended Byzantine hopes of relief before the siege had even begun. The fortress went up in four months before the siege of Constantinople, and each of its three great towers was assigned to a vizier, whose name it still carries.
outro: This brings our journey through Rumeli Fortress to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
